main_body: A square hay bale drawn as a flat panel with a vertical dark brown binding strap and a horizontal seam at row 8; it reads as a straight-on face rather than a box with a top and a front.
top_band: Rows 3-7 are light yellow (#d4b05c), but the tone is the same family as the face below (L 177 vs 153/134). The only step is a 1-row seam at row 8 (L116). This upper block is a face panel, not a top surface.
evidence: The bale is two stacked straw panels of about equal size, split by a thin dark seam at row 8, with a vertical strap through the middle. The upper half is only slightly lighter than the lower half (L177 vs 153/134), a difference under 25 L, so it is not a separate top surface. There is no foreshortened top band, no eave shadow and no inset detail; the strap and straw texture are painted flat. This is a front elevation, and a top that reads as a surface is missing.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. The outline is a tinted dark brown (0% neutral), which is good. The straw texture is a sparse pattern of alternating 2-tone dots, so the surface has little grain or clump variation. There are only about 4 lightness steps on the straw ramp. It is clearly thinner than the references.
